blocks.text: “ZECHARIAH, THE SON OF BERECHIAH, THE SON OF IDDO THE PROPHET” (ZECHARIAH 1:1) · EXILE & RETURN
Zechariah. Night visions in the second year of Darius; the fasts in the fourth; two burdens after.
The first word: Turn ye unto me
THE FIRST WORD: TURN YE UNTO ME
“Turn ye unto me, saith the LORD of hosts, and I will turn unto you, saith the LORD of hosts.”
He saw visions “by night”, and asked “the angel that talked with me” what they meant. Zechariah 1:8–9 Zechariah 1:19 Zechariah 4:1–5 Zechariah 5:5 Zechariah 6:4
He was told to take silver and gold from the returned exiles, make crowns and set them on the head of Joshua the high priest. Zechariah 6:9–15
He was told to “feed the flock of the slaughter” with two staves called Beauty and Bands, and later to take “the instruments of a foolish shepherd”. Zechariah 11:4–17
Chapters 9 and 12 open with “The burden of the word of the LORD”. Zechariah 9:1 Zechariah 12:1
When Sherezer and Regem-melech asked the priests and prophets whether to keep weeping in the fifth month, the word came to Zechariah. Zechariah 7:1–7
Ezra names him “Zechariah the son of Iddo” and says the elders “prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah”. Ezra 5:1 Ezra 6:14

Scholars' viewKeil (1868) takes this Darius to be Darius Hystaspes (Darius I): Zechariah, he writes, began “in the second year of Darius Hystaspes, only two months later than his contemporary Haggai”. On Parker and Dubberstein's tables (1942), the second year of Darius I ran from spring 520 BC to spring 519 BC, and his fourth year began in spring 518 BC. Zechariah 1:1 Zechariah 7:1 [37][24]
“In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, came the word of the LORD unto Zechariah”
“Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.”
The word in its main themes
“Be ye not as your fathers, unto whom the former prophets have cried”
Jealous for Jerusalem; the house shall be built
“I am returned to Jerusalem with mercies: my house shall be built in it, saith the LORD of hosts”
Not by might, nor by power
“Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.”
Judgment and mercy rather than fasts
“Execute true judgment, and shew mercy and compassions every man to his brother”
Many nations shall be joined to the LORD
“We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.”
“behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass”
“And the LORD shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one LORD, and his name one.”
To whom the word was spoken
“Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee”
“Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain”
TO THE PEOPLE OF THE LAND AND THE PRIESTS
“When ye fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh month, even those seventy years, did ye at all fast unto me, even to me?”
“Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee”
“The burden of the word of the LORD in the land of Hadrach, and Damascus shall be the rest thereof”
“Woe to the idol shepherd that leaveth the flock!”
The man among the myrtle trees
The candlestick and two olive trees
The two staves and the thirty pieces
8 The woman in the ephah Zechariah 5:5–11
WHERE THE NEW TESTAMENT QUOTES IT · 14
Each band joins a chapter of Zechariah to the New Testament books quoting it (6 books).
Who stood with him, and against him
The angel that talked with me

From the textZechariah's last dated word is in the fourth year of Darius; Ezra says the house was finished in the sixth year through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah. Scripture says nothing of his death. Zechariah 7:1 Ezra 6:14–15
G. L. Robinson writes in the ISBE that “nothing is known of his end. The Targum says he died a martyr.”[28] Who says so: The Targum, as reported in the ISBE, reported 1915
Grandson of Iddo, a priest who succeeded him as head of the house
C. F. Keil (1868); G. L. Robinson in ISBE (1915), conditionally

Keil holds that Zechariah “followed his grandfather in that office under the high priest Jehoiakim”, and that “his father died young”, which he thinks may explain why Ezra calls him “the son (grandson) of Iddo”. Robinson writes that the same Iddo “seems to be mentioned” in Nehemiah 12:4, and “if so, Zechariah was a priest as well as a prophet”. Zechariah 1:1 Ezra 5:1 Nehemiah 12:4 Nehemiah 12:16 [24][28]

Zechariah's book does not call him a priest; Nehemiah 12:16 names a Zechariah at the head of Iddo's priestly house.
The book gives no date for chapters 9–14.
Scripture does not say how or when Zechariah died.
